title: Derived forms of smooth base change
statement:
In the Cartesian square of [sk-thm-smooth-base-change], with $f$ smooth and
$g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $\mathcal P$ be the set of primes
invertible on the base. The base-change map of [sk-def-bc] is an isomorphism

$$
Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

for bounded constructible $K$ ([sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change]),
for bounded $\mathcal P$-torsion $K$ ([sbc-thm-bounded-allowable-torsion]), and
for every $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$
([sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change]). Each is reduced to the
degreewise statement of [sk-thm-smooth-base-change] by a finite-range
comparison and a truncation criterion.

blueprint_update.statement:
Consider a cartesian square with $u:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and
the exchange map $\operatorname{Ex}_{g,f}(K):g^*Rf_*K\to Rf'_*u^*K$ of
[sk-lem-sbc-exchange-compatibility].
Let $g$ be smooth and $f$ quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Let $\Lambda$ be a discrete commutative ring
annihilated by an integer $n$ invertible on $Y$. For every

$$
 K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)
$$

the canonical map $\operatorname{Ex}_{g,f}(K)$ is an isomorphism in
$D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(Y'_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$.

In particular, for a classical $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$ and all $q$,

$$
 g^*R^qf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qf'_*u^*F.
$$

*Complement.* In the Cartesian square of the complement of [sk-thm-smooth-base-change], with
$f$ smooth and $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $\mathcal P$ be the set of primes
invertible on the base. The base-change map of [sk-def-bc] is an isomorphism

$$
Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rh_*Le^*K
$$

for bounded constructible $K$ ([sbc-thm-bounded-derived-smooth-base-change]),
for bounded $\mathcal P$-torsion $K$ ([sbc-thm-bounded-allowable-torsion]), and
for every $K\in D^+_{\mathcal P\text{-tor}}(T_{\Et})$
([sbc-thm-bounded-below-derived-smooth-base-change]).

proof.text:
For a classical sheaf the assertion is
[sk-thm-smooth-base-change], applied to the underlying
abelian sheaf, which is killed by $n$. The exchange map is
$\Lambda$-linear by its unit–counit construction, so it is an
isomorphism of $\Lambda$-module sheaves.

For a complex, choose $a$ with $K\in D^{\geq a}$. The hypercohomology
spectral sequences of the two sides have terms

$$
 g^*R^pf_*H^q(K),\qquad R^pf'_*u^*H^q(K),
 \qquad p\geq0,\quad q\geq a,
$$

and the exchange map induces on them the sheaf comparison, an
isomorphism by the preceding paragraph. In each total degree only
finitely many pairs $(p,q)$ occur, so these shifted first-quadrant
spectral sequences converge and the map on abutments is an isomorphism;
alternatively, truncate $K$ above the relevant total degree first. Finally,
[sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and
[sk-cor-pe-classical-derived] show that the direct and inverse
images involved are classical, and
[sk-lem-sbc-exchange-compatibility] identifies the comparison with
the exchange map $\operatorname{Ex}_{g,f}(K)$.

*Complement.* Each of the three étale statements is reduced to the degreewise statement of
[sk-thm-smooth-base-change] by a finite-range comparison and a truncation criterion.
